source_text: 1. QuonramM autem non solum prophetze et justi multi, preescientes per Spiritum sanctum adventum ejus, orayerunt in illud tempus venire, in quo facie ad faciem viderent Dominum suum, et sermones audirent ejus, Dominus fecit manifestum, dicens discipulis: Multi prophet et justi cupierunt videre que videtis, et non viderunt, et audire que auditis, et non audierunt. Quemadmodum igitur concupierunt et audire, et videre, nisi preescissent futurum ejus adventum? Quomodo autem prescire potuerunt, nisi ab ipso preescientiam ante accepissent? Quomodo autem Scripture testificantur de eo, nisi ab uno et eodem Deo omnia semper per Verbum revelata et ostensa fuissent credentibus ; aliquando quidem colloquente eo cum suo plasmate, aliquando autem dante legem, aliquando vero exprobrante, aliquando vero exhortante, ac deinceps liberante servum, et adoptante in filium, et apto tempore incorruptele heereditatem prestante, ad perfectionem hominis? enim eum in augmentum et incrementum, quemadmodum et Scriptura dicit: Crescite et multiplicamini. 2. Et hoe Deus ab homine differt, quoniam Deus quidem facit, homo autem fit: et quidem qui facit, semper idem est: quod autem fit, et initium, et medietatem, et adjectionem, et augmentum accipere debet. Et Deus quidem bene facit, bene autem homini. Et Deus°quidem perfectus in omnibus, ipse sibi eequalis et similis; totus cum sit lumen, et totus mens, et totus substantia, et fons omnium bonorum: homo vero profectum percipiens et augmentum ad Deum. Quemadmodum enim Deus semper idem est; sic et homo in Deo inventus, semper proficiet Deum. Neque enim Deus cessat aliquando in benefaciendo, et locupletando hominem: neque homo cessat beneficium accipere, et ditari a Deo. Exceptorium enim bonitatis, et organum clarificationis ejus, homo gratus ei qui se fecit: et iterum exceptorium justi judicii ejus homo ingratus, et spernens plasmatorem, et non Verbo ejus: qui plurimum semper fructificantibus, et plus habentibus dominicum argentum, daturum se pollicitus est. Euge, inquit, serve bone, et fidelis, quia in modico fidelis fuisti, super multa te constituam; intra in gaudium Domini tui: ipse Dominus plurimum promittens. 98. Sieut ergo nune fructificantibus, plurimum daturum se pollicitus est, secundum munerationem gratize suze, sed non secundum commutationem agnitionis; ipse enim Dominus perseverat, et idem Pater revelatur; sic ergo et posterioribus majorem quam que fuit in veteri Testamento munerationem gratiz attriunus et idem Dominus per suum adyentum. Et illi enim per famulos audiebant venturum regem, et mediocriter gaudebant, secundum quod sperabant venturum eum: qui autem preesentem viderunt, et libertatem adepti et potiti sunt ejus muneratione, majorem gratiam et abundantiorem exultationem habent, gaude regis adventu, quemadmodum et David dicit: Anima mea exultabit in Domino, jucundabitur in salutari ejus. Et propter hoc Hierosolymam introéunte eo, omnes qui erant in via David, in dolore anime cognoverunt suum regem, et substraverunt ei vestimenta, et ramis viridibus adornaverunt viam, cum magna leetitia et exultatione clamantes: Osanna filio David, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Osanna in excelsis, Zelantibus autem malis dispensatoribus, qui circumyeniebant inferiores, et eorum quibus ratio non constabat, et propter hoe nolentibus venisse regem, et dicentibus ei, Audis quid isti dicunt? ait Dominus: Nunquam legistis, Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem? id quod a David in Filium Dei dietum érat, in se factum ostendens, et significans, illos quidem virtutem Scripture, et dispositionem Dei; se autem esse qui a prophetis annuntiatus sit Christus, cujus nomen in omni terra laudatur, ex ore infantium et lactentium laudem perficientis suo Patri: quapropter et elevata est magnificentia ejus super Si ergo idem ipse adest, qui preedicatus est a prophetis, Dominus noster Jesus Christus, et adventus ejus pleniorem gratiam et majorem munerationem attribuit his qui susceperunt eum, manifestum, quoniam et Pater idem ipse est, qui a prophetis annuntiatus est, et non alterius Patris agnitionem fecit veniens Filius, sed ejusdem qui ab initio preedicatus est; a quo et libertatem detulit his qui legitime, et prono animo, et’ toto corde deserviunt ei: contemtoribus autem, et non subjectis Deo, sed in gloriam hominum exteriores munditias sectantibus, (quee in figuram futurorum traditz erant, velut ®umbree cujusdam descriptionem Lege, atque deliniante de temporalibus zeterna, de terrenis ceelestia), fingentibus plusquam quz dicta sunt sese observare, tanquam diligentiam suam etiam ipsi Deo preeferentibus, intus autem plenis hypocrisi, et cupiditate, et omni malitia, sempiternam attulit perditionem, abscindens eos a vita.
pass_a_gloss: For when not only prophets and many righteous, foreseeing through the Holy Spirit His coming, prayed to come in that time in which they might see their Lord face to face, and hear His words, the Lord made manifest, saying to the disciples: Many prophets and righteous desired to see what you see, and did not see, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear. How therefore did they desire to hear and see, unless they had foreknown His coming? How however could they have foreknown, unless they had received foreknowledge from Him? How however do the Scriptures testify about Him, unless all things were always revealed and shown to believers through the Word by one and the same God; sometimes speaking with His creature, sometimes giving the law, sometimes rebuking, sometimes exhorting, and then liberating the servant, and adopting as a son, and at the suitable time granting an incorruptible inheritance, for the perfection of man? For He says to him for increase and growth, just as Scripture also says: Grow and multiply. And this God differs from man, because God indeed does, but man is done: and indeed He who does is always the same: but what is done receives beginning, and middle, and addition, and increase. And God indeed does good, but to man it is good. And God is perfect in all things, equal and similar to Himself; entirely light, and entirely mind, and entirely substance, and fountain of all goods: but man receives progress and increase toward God. For just as God is always the same, so also man found in God will always make progress toward God. For neither does God ever cease doing good and enriching man: nor does man cease receiving benefit and being enriched by God. For man is a receptacle of His goodness, and an organ of His clarification: grateful to Him who made him: and again a receptacle of His just judgment, man ungrateful and despising the Creator, and not obedient to His Word: who promised to give Himself to those always bearing much fruit, and having more, the Master's money. Well done, He says, good and faithful servant, because you were faithful in a small thing, I will set you over many things: enter into the joy of your Lord: the Lord Himself promising much. Thus as now to those bearing fruit, He promised to give much, according to the gift of His grace, but not according to a commutation of acknowledgment; for the Lord Himself perseveres, and the same Father is revealed: thus also to those later, a greater gift of grace than what was in the Old Testament is attributed to them, and the same Lord through His advent. And those indeed heard through servants that the King was coming, and they rejoiced moderately, according to what they hoped He would come: but those who saw Him present, and received and possessed His gift, have greater grace and more abundant exultation, rejoicing at the King's advent, just as David also says: My soul will exult in the Lord, it will be joyful in His Savior. And because of this, when He entered Jerusalem, all those who were on the way of David, in sorrow of soul recognized their King, and spread their garments under Him, and adorned the way with green branches, crying out with great joy and exultation: Hosanna to the Son of David, Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest. But to the evil dispensers, who were going around the lower ones, and whose reason was not constant, and because of this were unwilling for the King to come, and were saying to Him, Do You hear what these say? the Lord said: Have you never read, You perfected praise from the mouth of infants and nurslings? which was said by David about the Son of God, showing that it was done in Himself, and signifying that they indeed have the power of Scripture, and the disposition of God; but He is the Christ announced by the prophets, whose name is praised in all the earth, perfecting praise from the mouth of infants and nurslings to His Father: therefore His magnificence is also elevated above. If therefore He Himself is present, who was predicted by the prophets, our Lord Jesus Christ, and His advent attributes a fuller grace and greater gift to those who received Him, it is manifest that the Father is also the same, who was announced by the prophets, and the Son did not make known a different Father, but the same one who was predicted from the beginning; from whom He also brought freedom to those who serve Him lawfully, and with a prone soul, and with their whole heart: but to those contemptuous and not subject to God, but pursuing external purities for the glory of men, (which were handed down as a figure of future things, like a shadow of a certain description of the Law, and delineating eternal things from temporal ones, and heavenly things from earthly ones), feigning to observe more than what was said, as if they were preferring their diligence even to God, but inwardly full of hypocrisy, and cupidity, and all malice, He brought eternal perdition, cutting them off from life.

pass_b_english: Not only the prophets but also many righteous people foresaw Christ's coming through the Holy Spirit and prayed to live in the very time when they could see their Lord face to face and hear His words. The Lord Himself confirmed this, telling His disciples, "Many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it" (Matt. 13:17). How could they have longed to see and hear unless they had foreknown His coming? And how could they have foreknown it unless they had received that foreknowledge from Him? How else do the Scriptures testify about Him unless one and the same God has always revealed and shown all things to believers through the Word? At one time He spoke with His creature; at another He gave the law; at another He rebuked; at another He exhorted; then He liberated the servant and adopted him as a son; and at the proper time He granted an incorruptible inheritance for the perfection of man. Indeed, He says this to humanity for its increase and growth, just as Scripture says, "Grow and multiply" (Gen. 1:28).

This is how God differs from man: God acts, but man is acted upon. The One who acts is always the same, whereas what is acted upon must receive beginning, middle, addition, and increase. God does good, and it is good for man. God is perfect in all things, equal and like to Himself—entirely light, entirely mind, entirely substance, the fountain of all good things—while man receives progress and increase toward God. For just as God is always the same, so also the man who is found in God will always make progress toward God. Neither does God ever cease doing good and enriching man, nor does man cease receiving benefit and being enriched by God. Man is a receptacle of God's goodness and an organ of His clarification, grateful to the One who made him. But man is also a receptacle of His just judgment when he is ungrateful, despises his Creator, and disobeys His Word. To those who always bear much fruit and have more, the Master promised to give His own money. "Well done, good and faithful servant," He says. "Because you were faithful in a small matter, I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your Lord" (Matt. 25:21, 23)—the Lord Himself promising much.

Therefore, just as He now promises to give much to those who bear fruit according to the measure of His grace, not according to any exchange of acknowledgment—for the Lord perseveres, and the same Father is revealed—so also to those who came later He attributed a greater gift of grace than what existed in the Old Testament, and the same Lord did this through His advent. In the former time, people heard through servants that the King was coming, and they rejoiced moderately, according to what they hoped. But those who saw Him present, who received and took possession of His gift, have greater grace and more abundant exultation, rejoicing at the King's advent, just as David says: "My soul will exult in the Lord; it will rejoice in His salvation" (Ps. 35:9). Because of this, when He entered Jerusalem, all who were on the road—those of David's line—in the sorrow of their souls recognized their King. They spread their garments before Him and adorned the way with green branches, crying out with great joy and exultation: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!" (Matt. 21:9). But the evil stewards, who lorded it over the lowly—those whose reasoning was not steadfast and who therefore did not want the King to come—said to Him, "Do you hear what these are saying?" The Lord answered, "Have you never read: 'From the mouths of infants and nursing babies You have perfected praise'?" (Matt. 21:16; Ps. 8:2). This was spoken by David concerning the Son of God, showing that it was fulfilled in Him and signifying that these children indeed possessed the power of Scripture and the disposition of God. But He is the Christ announced by the prophets, whose name is praised in all the earth, perfecting praise from the mouths of infants and nursing babies to His Father. Therefore His magnificence is also exalted above.

If, then, He Himself is present—the One predicted by the prophets, our Lord Jesus Christ—and His advent bestows a fuller grace and a greater gift on those who received Him, it is manifest that the Father is also the same One announced by the prophets. The Son did not make known a different Father by His coming, but the same One who was proclaimed from the beginning. From Him, Christ brought freedom to those who serve Him lawfully, with a willing soul and their whole heart. But to those who are contemptuous and not subject to God—who pursue external purities for the glory of men (things handed down as a figure of future realities, like a shadowy outline of the Law, delineating eternal things from temporal ones and heavenly things from earthly ones), who feign to observe more than what was commanded as if they were putting their own diligence above God, while inwardly they are full of hypocrisy, greed, and every malice—He brought eternal perdition, cutting them off from life.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the distinction between God who 'does' (facit) and man who 'is done' (fit). All scripture citations in Pass B (Matt 13:17, Gen 1:28, Matt 25:21, 23, Ps 35:9, Matt 21:9, Matt 21:16, Ps 8:2) are appropriate identifications of the quoted or alluded-to Latin text. The translation of 'argentum dominicum' as 'the Master's money' in Pass A and 'His own money' in Pass B is a faithful rendering of the Latin. The complex parenthetical regarding the Law as a shadow is preserved.
